fact: Telecom Namibia signed a master service agreement with Angola Telecom and SATCAB to integrate the Southern African Regional Submarine System (SARSSy) with the Equiano cable via Telecom Namibia's Swakopmund landing station, with Telecom Namibia as landing party and giving Angola Telecom 1 Tbps on Equiano; it builds on an MoU and commercial terms agreement signed in April 2026.

fact: Telecom Namibia, Angola Telecom and SATCAB signed the master service agreement for SARSSy on 12 June 2026, integrating it with the Equiano cable; Telecom Namibia as landing party hosts the infrastructure in Namibia and provides an initial 1.0 Tbps on Equiano, building on an April 2026 MoU and commercial terms agreement signed in Swakopmund.

Telecom Namibia entered a pilot commercial agreement with Angola's GGPEN, finalised at the ANGOTIC forum in Luanda, for a real-network trial of Angosat-2 services, with full commercial launch targeted after the pilot (published 2026-06-12).

Namibia's ICT ministry partnered with Angola, through Telecom Namibia and GGPEN, to use the Angosat-2 satellite for remote-area connectivity; discussions began in June 2025 and a proof of concept was launched (published 2025-10-14, which is the date used).

Broadband Infraco, South Africa's state wholesaler, said in July 2019 that its regional network provides connectivity to all six neighbouring countries, Namibia among them, and acts as the gateway to international capacity for South Africa's landlocked neighbours.
